Incident Name: Silverwood Reservoir Crude Oil Pipeline Rupture
4 MapSketch include sketch showing the t: North-oriented map of a 4.0-mile radius covering Trans-California Pipeline MM 87.3, Sawpit Canyon, and Silverwood Reservoir. The primary site is Valve Station 12, where a 12-inch crude line ruptured. Impacts include 800 yards of creek bed and a 30-acre sheen in the reservoir South arm. Threatened sites are the Mojave Water Agency Pumping Plant 1.5 miles North and State Recreation Area campgrounds 0.8 miles West. Cal FIRE Recon Aircraft 240 observed crude pooling in the canyon and a 400-yard-wide oil ribbon entering the lake. The slick moves North at 1.0 knot; VOCs move Southeast at 7 mph. About 1.2 miles of rocky shoreline and marsh are impacted. Show Staging Area Delta at the marina, the Command Post at Hesperia Fire Station 30, a 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone, Boom Sites A and B, and intake protection zones.
5 Situation Summary and Health and Safet: At 12:40, land movement ruptured the pipeline, discharging about 12,000 gallons of heavy crude into Sawpit Canyon before automated valves stopped flow. Hazards include benzene and VOC inhalation, flammability at a 65°F flash point, wildfire ignition, oily-terrain falls, and heat exhaustion at 94°F. Enforce a 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone; require Level B with SCBA for initial creek entry and Level C with organic-vapor respirators for shoreline teams; continuously monitor downwind air with PIDs; maintain a wildland fire standby team with AFFF foam; and establish dual-basin wash decontamination at Marina Ramp 2.
7 Current and Planned Objectives: Enforce the 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone and secure pipeline isolation by 14:00; deploy 2,000 feet of boom across Sawpit Canyon inlet by 16:30; evacuate the State Recreation Area campgrounds by 15:00; start skimmer-boat recovery in the reservoir South arm by 17:00; and establish Unified Command by 14:30.
ActionsRow1: San Bernardino County Fire Engine 30 and USFS Crew 4 responded and established the initial safety perimeter.
ActionsRow2: Chief M. Thorne established Local Command; pipeline operators confirmed remote valve isolation at MM 85 and MM 90.
ActionsRow3: State Parks Rangers completed evacuation of 150 visitors from Silverwood Lake campgrounds.
ActionsRow4: Cal OES and the EPA OSC arrived; Unified Command was established at Station 30.
ActionsRow5: Clean Harbors Spill Response Vessel deployed 1,200 feet of hard boom at Sawpit Inlet, Boom Site A.
ActionsRow6: Deploy a secondary sorbent deflection-boom array at Boom Site B upstream of the Mojave Water Intake.
ActionsRow7: Vacuum skimmer vessel Lake Clean 1 initiates crude-oil recovery in the South arm.
ActionsRow8: Complete the initial shoreline oiling assessment along Sawpit Canyon inlet.
